geo.title: Get started
geo.body:
Patty-paper fold first, then compass.

Goal: I can construct a segment bisector and an angle bisector and give an informal reason why they work (formal proof in 4.13).

slides.title: The big idea
slides.html:
A segment bisector passes through a segment's midpoint. The perpendicular bisector also meets it at a right angle. An angle bisector is the ray that splits an angle into two equal angles.

To bisect AB: with the compass opened more than half of AB, draw arcs from A and from B. They cross at two points; the line through them is the perpendicular bisector. Informal reason: each crossing point is the same distance from A as from B. To bisect an angle, mark equal distances on both sides from the vertex, then draw equal arcs from those marks; the ray to their crossing bisects the angle. We prove both in 4.13.

slides.title: Check yourself
slides.html: Why must the compass be opened more than half of AB?
slides.reveal: If it is opened less than half, the two arcs do not reach each other, so they never cross.

slides.title: Common mistake
slides.html:
A student says: Bisecting means drawing any line through the middle by eye.
